headline: Egypt beat Australia on penalties to reach World Cup last 16
summary: In a historic first, Egypt advances to the knockout stages after a tense 4-2 penalty shootout victory in Texas.
details: Egypt made history by defeating Australia 4-2 on penalties to reach the World Cup last 16 for the first time. The match, held in Texas, ended 1-1 after 120 minutes of intense play.
Hossam Abdelmaguid scored the decisive penalty to secure the win. Mohamed Salah, returning from a hamstring strain, scored a 'cheeky chipped penalty' to boost his team's confidence.
Emam Ashour opened the scoring for Egypt in the 13th minute with a header. Australia equalized ten minutes after halftime through a Mohamed Hany own goal.
The shootout was marked by drama, as Australia's Harry Souttar missed the first penalty and 18-year-old Lucas Herrington hit the bar.
Egypt now faces reigning champions Argentina and Lionel Messi in the next round, provided Argentina avoids an upset against Cape Verde.
Captain Mohamed Salah was emotional after the match, stating that winning a World Cup knockout game is 'history' for his country.
caption:
History made! 🇪🇬 Egypt edges Australia in a nail-biting penalty shootout to storm into the World Cup last 16.

Egypt made history by defeating Australia 4-2 on penalties to reach the World Cup last 16 for the first time. The match, held in Texas, ended 1-1 after 120 minutes of intense play.

Hossam Abdelmaguid scored the decisive penalty to secure the win. Mohamed Salah, returning from a hamstring strain, scored a 'cheeky chipped penalty' to boost his team's confidence.

Emam Ashour opened the scoring for Egypt in the 13th minute with a header. Australia equalized ten minutes after halftime through a Mohamed Hany own goal.

The shootout was marked by drama, as Australia's Harry Souttar missed the first penalty and 18-year-old Lucas Herrington hit the bar.

Egypt now faces reigning champions Argentina and Lionel Messi in the next round, provided Argentina avoids an upset against Cape Verde.

Captain Mohamed Salah was emotional after the match, stating that winning a World Cup knockout game is 'history' for his country.

headline_marked: Messi makes history as [[first player to reach 30 World Cup appearances]]
headline: Messi makes history as first player to reach 30 World Cup appearances
summary: Lionel Messi returns to Argentina's starting lineup for their last-32 clash against Cape Verde, extending his legendary tournament record.
details: Captain Lionel Messi returns to the starting lineup for Argentina in their World Cup last-32 match against tournament debutants Cape Verde on Friday.
With this start, Messi becomes the first player in history to make 30 appearances at the World Cup, further cementing his status as the tournament's all-time top scorer.
The match also marks a significant milestone for Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni, who is celebrating his 100th game in charge of the national team since 2018.
In the attacking lineup, Lautaro Martinez joins Messi, while Julian Alvarez has been benched for this encounter.
For Cape Verde, midfielder Telmo Arcanjo remains on the bench due to a leg injury, while left-back Sidny Lopes Cabral returns to the starting eleven after a one-match suspension.

Argentina's starting XI includes Emiliano Martinez, Lisandro Martinez, Cristian Romero, Facundo Medina, Nahuel Molina, Rodrigo De Paul, Alexis Mac Allister, Enzo Fernandez, Lionel Messi, Thiago Almada, and Lautaro Martinez.
caption:
30 World Cup matches. A record that only one man has ever reached.

Captain Lionel Messi returns to the starting lineup for Argentina in their World Cup last-32 match against tournament debutants Cape Verde on Friday.

The match also marks a significant milestone for Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni, who is celebrating his 100th game in charge of the national team since 2018.

In the attacking lineup, Lautaro Martinez joins Messi, while Julian Alvarez has been benched for this encounter.

For Cape Verde, midfielder Telmo Arcanjo remains on the bench due to a leg injury, while left-back Sidny Lopes Cabral returns to the starting eleven after a one-match suspension.

Argentina's starting XI includes Emiliano Martinez, Lisandro Martinez, Cristian Romero, Facundo Medina, Nahuel Molina, Rodrigo De Paul, Alexis Mac Allister, Enzo Fernandez, Lionel Messi, Thiago Almada, and Lautaro Martinez.
